verses.text: So you’re out here judging somebody else while doing the same stuff? No excuse, fam—you just called yourself out.
We know God’s judgment lands on people doing this in line with the truth.
Do you really think you’ll dodge God’s judgment while you’re judging others for the same things you do?
Or are you taking God’s kindness, patience, and restraint for granted? Don’t you see his kindness is trying to lead you back to him? 👀
Your stubborn, unrepentant heart is stacking up judgment for yourself for the day God brings his anger and fair verdict into the open.
God “will repay each person for what they’ve done.”
To the people who keep doing good and seek glory, honor, and a life that won’t fade, he’ll give eternal life.
But if you’re chasing your own agenda, rejecting truth, and going along with injustice, you’re lining up for anger and fury.
There’ll be suffering and distress for everyone doing evil—the Jew first, and also the Greek.
But everyone doing good will receive glory, honor, and peace—the Jew first, and also the Greek.
God doesn’t play favorites. Not even a little.
People who sin without the Law will perish without it. People who sin under the Law will be judged by it.
Just hearing the Law doesn’t make you right with God. The ones who actually do what it says will be declared right.
(When Gentiles who don’t have the Law naturally do what it asks, they become a law to themselves, even without possessing it.
They show the Law’s demands written on their hearts. Their conscience backs it up, and their thoughts go back and forth, accusing them or defending them.)
That’ll all come to light on the day God judges people’s hidden lives through Jesus Christ. That’s part of the Good News I preach.
So, you call yourself Jewish, lean on the Law, and brag about God,
you know what he wants and can spot what matters because the Law taught you—
you’re sure you can guide the blind and shine light for people in the dark,
correct the foolish and teach the young, because the Law gives you the outline of knowledge and truth—
but do you teach yourself, teacher? You preach, “Don’t steal,” so are you stealing?
You say, “Don’t commit adultery,” but do you? You can’t stand idols, but are you robbing temples?
You brag about the Law, then disrespect God by breaking it?
Scripture says, “Because of you, God’s name gets dragged among the Gentiles.”
Circumcision helps if you actually keep the Law. But if you break it, that mark counts for nothing.
So if an uncircumcised person keeps the Law’s requirements, won’t God count them as circumcised?
Won’t the person without the physical mark who fulfills the Law judge you, who have the written Law and circumcision but still break the Law?
Being Jewish isn’t just an outside label. Circumcision isn’t just a mark on your body.
The real Jew is Jewish on the inside. Real circumcision happens in the heart, by the Spirit—not just by the written code. That person gets praise from God, not people.
